My highest value school is y, and I have top priority there. Therefore, I am very likely to get y if I rank it first. However, let's consider the possibility of strategically ranking other schools higher.

If I rank y second, I will likely still get it because I have top priority there. This strategy would only make sense if I thought I had a reasonable chance of getting x.

Since most applicants prefer y > x > w > z, it's likely that x will be competitive. I have priority 2 at x. If many students rank x highly, it's possible I won't get it. In that case, I would move to y.

If I rank w first, I have priority 1 there, so I am likely to get it. However, y is worth much more to me, so I don't want to do this.

If I rank z first, I have priority 2 there. I also don't want to do this, as it is my least preferred school.

Ranking y first guarantees me y, which is the best outcome I can reasonably expect. Therefore, I will rank y first.

Now, what should I rank second? I should rank my next most preferred school, which is x. If I don't get y, I want to have a chance at x.

After x, I prefer w over z. Therefore, I will rank w before z.

Therefore, my optimal ranking is y > x > w > z.
